sequence_description: Token exchange attempts to validate a subject_token under the wrong connector_id (trust-anchor substitution via connector selection). Dex must bind verification policy to the intended connector and reject tokens that do not validate under that connector.
description: [LLM-Judge] Test is invalid/inconclusive: control login failed (password grant unsupported), so the run does not demonstrate connector_id trust-anchor substitution or cross-connector validation behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Test is invalid/inconclusive: control login failed (password grant unsupported), so the run does not demonstrate connector_id trust-anchor substitution or cross-connector validation behavior.

sequence_description: Authorization code flow control followed by an attacker attempting to redeem the same code with incorrect client_secret (simulating untrusted client attempting to 'resign' the proof at token endpoint). Dex must reject redemption without correct client authentication.
description: [LLM-Judge] Control authorization-code redemption failed with invalid_grant, so the test cannot confirm whether Dex would correctly bind the code to the legitimate client before evaluating the wrong-secret attack.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Control authorization-code redemption failed with invalid_grant, so the test cannot confirm whether Dex would correctly bind the code to the legitimate client before evaluating the wrong-secret attack.

sequence_description: I4: Use OIDC authorization request with id_token_hint and login_hint to attempt principal confusion/collision across two distinct upstream principals (hint-based subject override).
description: [LLM-Judge] Two distinct login attempts (user_A vs user_B) resulted in the exact same subject/entity identity, indicating possible principal confusion or a misconfigured/mock connector collapsing users into one account.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Two distinct login attempts (user_A vs user_B) resulted in the exact same subject/entity identity, indicating possible principal confusion or a misconfigured/mock connector collapsing users into one account.

sequence_description: I4: Use OIDC authorization request with id_token_hint and login_hint to attempt principal confusion/collision across two distinct upstream principals (hint-based subject override).
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization code exchange failed with invalid_grant for both flows, yet /userinfo succeeded for both sessions; this suggests the test may be using an existing session token or mixing sessions, making the principal-confusion result hard to attribute to the id_token_hint/login_hint behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization code exchange failed with invalid_grant for both flows, yet /userinfo succeeded for both sessions; this suggests the test may be using an existing session token or mixing sessions, making the principal-confusion result hard to attribute to the id_token_hint/login_hint behavior.

sequence_description: I4: Token exchange with subject_token_type confusion (present same opaque subject_token under different subject_token_type values) to probe identity mapping collisions.
description: [LLM-Judge] Distinct test identities (user_A vs user_B) resulted in the same issued subject/entity_id and identical userinfo (name/email), suggesting identity mapping collision or the test harness is not actually varying the upstream subject during token exchange.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Distinct test identities (user_A vs user_B) resulted in the same issued subject/entity_id and identical userinfo (name/email), suggesting identity mapping collision or the test harness is not actually varying the upstream subject during token exchange.

sequence_description: I4: Token exchange with subject_token_type confusion (present same opaque subject_token under different subject_token_type values) to probe identity mapping collisions.
description: [LLM-Judge] Password grant attempts failed with unsupported_grant_type, yet later fields indicate login_success=200 for both users, implying inconsistent result recording that could invalidate the security conclusion of this sequence.

sequence_description: Attempt to escalate claims/permissions by exchanging a limited-scope token for a broader-scope token via RFC 8693 token exchange.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange succeeded even though the control authorization-code flow failed to obtain any token, so the scope-escalation result is not attributable to exchanging a limited-scope token and may indicate missing subject_token validation or a test/setup flaw.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange succeeded even though the control authorization-code flow failed to obtain any token, so the scope-escalation result is not attributable to exchanging a limited-scope token and may indicate missing subject_token validation or a test/setup flaw.

sequence_description: Token exchange: present the same subject_token under different subject_token_type values to probe type confusion leading to over-grant (e.g., treating access_token as id_token). Includes control exchange.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange produced materially different userinfo/authorization attributes for the same subject (same sub/entity_id) between control and type-confused runs, suggesting subject_token_type confusion or inconsistent claim-to-authorization mapping.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange produced materially different userinfo/authorization attributes for the same subject (same sub/entity_id) between control and type-confused runs, suggesting subject_token_type confusion or inconsistent claim-to-authorization mapping.

sequence_description: Cross-subject token exchange: obtain a subject_token as user A, then attempt to exchange it while authenticated as user B (or a different session context) to see if Dex issues a token bound to the wrong principal or grants unintended permissions.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange succeeded even though both user A and user B authorization-code control flows failed (no valid subject_token was obtained), suggesting the exchange may not be bound to the intended upstream subject token/user context or the test setup is inconsistent.
